contract: Explicit outer-card inventories; Practical, Engineering, and Empirical are internal inspection layers; custody and greater Laws navigation remain outside the carousel.

cards.label: Source
cards.summary: Identify the event or condition that produces the reading.
cards.practical: Name the real change before treating its display or report as the change itself.
cards.engineering: Declare the source state, sampling point, timestamp, and ownership of the originating measurement.
cards.empirical: Require records that connect the observed reading to the named source under comparable conditions.

cards.label: Channel
cards.summary: Inspect how the reading travels from source to receiver.
cards.practical: Show where the signal can be delayed, lost, distorted, or detached from its context.
cards.engineering: Specify transport, latency, missingness, saturation, synchronization, and channel failure behavior.
cards.empirical: Compare transmitted and received records and preserve dropped, duplicated, and late observations.

cards.label: Detection
cards.summary: Define what makes a change observable enough to warrant attention.
cards.practical: Explain what a person or operator would notice and what decision that observation could support.
cards.engineering: Fix the observation process, feature construction, event horizon, receiver state, and detection rule.
cards.empirical: Report detection performance on records excluded from development, including observation counts and comparators.

cards.label: Noise and Threshold
cards.summary: Separate meaningful movement from variation, drift, and threshold artifacts.
cards.practical: Show why a moved display may still be noise and why a quiet display may still hide change.
cards.engineering: Declare noise assumptions, calibration, drift, threshold sensitivity, false positives, and false negatives.
cards.empirical: Test alternative thresholds and preserve uncertainty, error rates, and negative results.

cards.label: Interpretation
cards.summary: Bound what a trustworthy signal does and does not explain.
cards.practical: Translate the reading into an inspectable warning without turning warning into certainty.
cards.engineering: Keep detection, classification, causal explanation, and action policy as separate system states.
cards.empirical: The battery result supports bounded held-out ranking of the defined near-term event, not a distinct mechanism or universal signal law.
cards.boundary: A signal can support attention without proving cause, mechanism, transfer, or deployment fitness.

cards.label: Return Signal
cards.summary: Identify what came back from the result.
cards.practical: Show the observed outcome that becomes information for a later action.
cards.engineering: Declare the feedback path, observation state, sampling point, and returned value.
cards.empirical: Require an observed return signal rather than inferring feedback from event order alone.

cards.label: Controller
cards.summary: Name who or what receives the return and can respond.
cards.practical: Identify the person, rule, or mechanism capable of changing what happens next.
cards.engineering: Specify controller authority, decision function, state, limits, and unavailable inputs.
cards.empirical: Preserve records showing the controller received the signal before an adjustment occurred.

cards.label: Adjustment
cards.summary: Inspect the revised input, action, allocation, or setting.
cards.practical: Make the consequence of the return signal visible in the next action.
cards.engineering: Record the commanded change, gain, saturation, bounds, and resulting system input.
cards.empirical: Compare intended and executed adjustments and preserve missing or partial execution.

cards.label: Delay
cards.summary: Treat timing as part of the loop, not as decoration.
cards.practical: Explain how a response arriving too late can reverse the value of feedback.
cards.engineering: Measure observation, decision, transport, and actuation latency and their effect on phase.
cards.empirical: Use timestamps to distinguish prompt response, lag, oscillation, and unrelated later change.

cards.label: Stability
cards.summary: Determine whether the loop dampens, amplifies, or destabilizes change.
cards.practical: Show whether repeated response settles the system or makes the problem grow.
cards.engineering: Inspect loop gain, saturation, oscillation, runaway paths, and stop conditions.
cards.empirical: Observe successive states and alternative explanations before calling the path stabilizing or destabilizing.
cards.boundary: Temporal return does not prove a functioning feedback mechanism unless the return path and resulting change are observed.

cards.label: Transfer Object
cards.summary: Name the object, service, instruction, or responsibility that changes hands.
cards.practical: Keep the transferred thing identifiable before, during, and after movement.
cards.engineering: Declare payload identity, schema, version, owner, completeness, and integrity checks.
cards.empirical: Compare sent and received objects and preserve loss, mutation, duplication, and ambiguity.

cards.label: State and Context
cards.summary: Carry the information the receiver needs to continue correctly.
cards.practical: A handoff includes what has happened, what remains open, and why the next action matters.
cards.engineering: Package current state, prior decisions, timing, dependencies, assumptions, and unresolved conditions.
cards.empirical: Inspect whether missing context predicts delay, rework, error, or discontinuity after transfer.

cards.label: Interface
cards.summary: Inspect the boundary through which custody moves.
cards.practical: Show the actual point where sender and receiver meet and where transfer can fail.
cards.engineering: Specify protocol, units, translation, capacity, timeout, retry, ordering, and compatibility.
cards.empirical: Measure latency, rejected states, transfer loss, protocol errors, and recovery behavior.

cards.label: Acceptance
cards.summary: Distinguish sending from the receiver's explicit readiness and agreement.
cards.practical: The receiver must be able to identify, understand, and take responsibility for the object.
cards.engineering: Define receiver readiness, validation gates, acceptance conditions, rejection, and rollback.
cards.empirical: Preserve acceptance or rejection events and verify that acknowledged state matches received state.

cards.label: Receipt and Continuity
cards.summary: Prove the transfer completed and the next state remained viable.
cards.practical: Show who holds responsibility now and whether work or service can continue.
cards.engineering: Bind receipt identity, timestamp, custody change, next-state initialization, and recovery path.
cards.empirical: Trace post-acceptance continuity, dropped responsibility, duplicate work, and later custody disputes.

cards.label: Failure Boundary
cards.summary: Keep transport, receipt, preserved meaning, and successful continuation distinct.
cards.practical: A moved item is not a successful handoff when the receiver cannot continue from it.
cards.engineering: Expose independent failure at send, transport, receive, validation, acceptance, receipt, and next state.
cards.empirical: No current study is admitted for this route; its standing remains conceptual and procedural.
cards.boundary: Movement alone is not a successful handoff; meaning, state, custody, and acceptance must be preserved.

cards.label: Audit
cards.boundary: Audit remains an inspection subject on this page; no separate Audit route is invented.

cards.label: Candidate Model
cards.summary: State the proposed explanation without presenting it as an observed fact.
cards.practical: Explain the real-world question the model is intended to clarify.
cards.engineering: Declare variables, mechanism, structure, and the relationships the model asserts.
cards.empirical: Separate observations that fit the model from observations that merely fail to distinguish it.

cards.label: Assumptions
cards.summary: Expose the conditions the explanation requires.
cards.practical: Name what must already be true for the explanation to make sense.
cards.engineering: Record fixed conditions, omitted variables, independence assumptions, and scope restrictions.
cards.empirical: Mark assumptions as observed, supported, untested, contradicted, or structurally required.

cards.label: Predictions
cards.summary: Specify what should be observed if the model is correct.
cards.practical: Translate the theory into visible differences a person could recognize.
cards.engineering: Freeze predicted direction, timing, scale, conditions, and comparison before evaluation.
cards.empirical: Compare predictions with held-out observation and preserve misses as well as matches.

cards.label: Rival Explanations
cards.summary: Keep simpler and incompatible explanations present.
cards.practical: Ask what else could produce the same apparent pattern.
cards.engineering: Define rival models, confounds, ablations, and discriminating tests.
cards.empirical: Evidence that fits several rivals does not identify a unique mechanism.

cards.label: Falsification
cards.summary: Name the outcome that would revise or reject the proposal.
cards.practical: Make it possible for the explanation to be wrong.
cards.engineering: Declare rejection, revision, hold, and retest conditions before observing the result.
cards.empirical: Preserve contradicting and non-discriminating outcomes rather than editing them into support.
cards.boundary: A theory can organize observations without being validated, causal, unique, or universally applicable.

cards.label: Observation
cards.summary: Identify what was directly seen, recorded, or measured.
cards.practical: Describe the observation in terms connected to the real problem.
cards.engineering: Declare unit, timestamp, sampling frame, missingness, and transformation state.
cards.empirical: Separate direct observation from derived indicator and interpretation.

cards.label: Provenance
cards.summary: Trace the observation to an admitted source.
cards.practical: Show where the record came from and why it belongs in the question.
cards.engineering: Preserve source identity, version, transformation, admission rule, and custody.
cards.empirical: Source existence alone does not establish relevance, reliability, or causal support.

cards.label: Weight
cards.summary: Classify how directly the evidence bears on the claim.
cards.practical: Distinguish strong support from a suggestive clue.
cards.engineering: Expose dependency, comparator structure, precision, and sensitivity to analysis choices.
cards.empirical: Classify support as direct, indirect, mixed, negative, absent, or unresolved.

cards.label: Alternatives
cards.summary: Keep ordinary explanations and negative evidence visible.
cards.practical: Ask whether a simpler account fits the same observations.
cards.engineering: Run comparator, ablation, confound, and threshold challenges.
cards.empirical: Preserve stronger alternatives and failed proposed measures alongside positive results.

cards.label: Evidentiary Standing
cards.summary: State the strongest claim the admitted record can carry.
cards.practical: Tell the reader what can responsibly be used and what remains open.
cards.engineering: Bind claim state to exact evidence, population, horizon, and validation condition.
cards.empirical: Bounded support does not prove mechanism, generality, operational value, or a universal law.
cards.boundary: Evidence may support a bounded relationship without proving mechanism, generality, or operational value.

cards.label: Quantity
cards.summary: Define the thing being measured before discussing its number.
cards.practical: Give observers one shared meaning for the quantity.
cards.engineering: Declare construct, variable, unit, scale, and valid range.
cards.empirical: Show that the recorded value corresponds to the declared quantity.

cards.label: Instrument
cards.summary: Identify how the world becomes a recorded value.
cards.practical: Show where observation depends on a device, procedure, or human classification.
cards.engineering: Specify sensor, collection procedure, sampling frame, resolution, and failure behavior.
cards.empirical: Preserve missingness, saturation, observer effects, and instrument-specific error.

cards.label: Calibration
cards.summary: Make different observations comparable.
cards.practical: Explain why the same world should not yield different classifications without notice.
cards.engineering: Declare reference, normalization, threshold, aggregation, and zero-value handling.
cards.empirical: Check calibration against known conditions and report drift or recalibration.

cards.label: Uncertainty
cards.summary: Keep precision and confidence inside the measurement record.
cards.practical: Show what the number cannot resolve.
cards.engineering: Represent error, interval, sensitivity, rounding, and boundary cases.
cards.empirical: Report uncertainty and threshold sensitivity with the result, not after it.

cards.label: Comparison
cards.summary: Interpret a metric only against its population, event, and comparator.
cards.practical: Connect the number to a bounded decision without turning ranking into mechanism.
cards.engineering: Bind metric definition, event horizon, split, comparator, and observation count.
cards.empirical: Preserve the battery combined AUROC 0.9394 beside the stronger burden comparator AUROC 0.9704.
cards.boundary: A metric is inseparable from its target, population, comparator, and unresolved transfer conditions.

cards.label: Supported Scope
cards.summary: Name the population, environment, horizon, and claim actually supported.
cards.practical: Tell the reader where the result can responsibly inform attention.
cards.engineering: Bind the claim to tested cases, inputs, target, split, and operating conditions.
cards.empirical: Preserve exact observation counts and validation state.

cards.label: Unknowns
cards.summary: Keep unresolved conditions visible beside the result.
cards.practical: State what the reader still cannot know.
cards.engineering: List unmeasured confounds, transfer gaps, missing controls, and unavailable regimes.
cards.empirical: Unknown is not negative evidence, and absence of contradiction is not support.

cards.label: Prohibited Claims
cards.summary: Separate unsupported promotion from bounded interpretation.
cards.practical: Name the conclusion a reader must not take away.
cards.engineering: Encode the claim ceiling and block mechanism, universality, safety, or deployment promotion.
cards.empirical: A held-out association does not by itself validate a distinct causal mechanism or critical-system use.

cards.label: Required Next Evidence
cards.summary: Identify what would be needed to move the boundary.
cards.practical: Show the next question rather than implying the answer is already present.
cards.engineering: Specify replication, controls, calibration, external population, and operational test requirements.
cards.empirical: Only newly admitted evidence can change the standing; presentation and routing cannot.

cards.label: Claim Ceiling
cards.summary: Preserve the strongest permitted public statement.
cards.practical: Make the stopping point understandable without hiding the useful result.
cards.engineering: Attach disposition, evidence locator, unresolved risks, and review condition.
cards.empirical: The ceiling remains the evidence-supported statement, while higher claims remain unresolved or prohibited.
cards.boundary: The strongest public statement is the evidence-supported claim ceiling; everything above it remains unresolved or prohibited.

cards.label: Route Custody
cards.summary: Keep the historical address without creating a second study owner.
cards.practical: Use this route to choose the correct Laws interpretation or complete Frontier record.
cards.engineering: Preserve compatibility routing, canonical ownership, and stable links.
cards.empirical: The wrapper creates no new observation, metric, or evidence standing.

cards.label: Laws Interpretation
cards.summary: Read theory, evidence, measure, findings, and limits as bounded Laws subjects.
cards.practical: Start with the question the result may help answer.
cards.engineering: Keep each conceptual and evidentiary layer separate.
cards.empirical: No contextual presentation upgrades the selected study.

cards.label: Frontier Record
cards.summary: Open the complete execution record at its canonical owner.
cards.practical: Use Frontier for the full study rather than a duplicate summary.
cards.engineering: Inspect design, held-out split, metrics, comparator, and execution context.
cards.empirical: The complete record remains the source for the 1,653 observations and all reported metrics.

cards.label: Preserved Result
cards.summary: Keep the positive result and stronger ordinary comparator together.
cards.practical: The study may support attention to battery health inside the tested domain.
cards.engineering: The defined event used a 20-cycle horizon across three held-out cells.
cards.empirical: Combined AUROC was 0.9394; burden comparator AUROC was 0.9704 and remained stronger.

cards.label: Compatibility Boundary
cards.summary: Prevent a continuity wrapper from becoming a second canonical study.
cards.practical: The address remains useful without changing the conclusion.
cards.engineering: Do not fork ownership, metric identity, evidence status, or claim ceiling.
cards.empirical: No new study is admitted by retaining the route.
cards.boundary: No metric, result, evidence status, ownership, or claim ceiling is changed by this wrapper.

cards.label: Evidence and Sources
cards.summary: Inspect datasets, provenance, observations, exclusions, and source-matching boundaries.
cards.practical: Find what the research can actually know from admitted material.
cards.engineering: Preserve source identity, custody, transformations, and admission rules.
cards.empirical: Source volume and existence do not by themselves validate a claim.

cards.label: Methods and Models
cards.summary: Inspect formulas, assumptions, normalization, comparison rules, and limitations.
cards.practical: Use the Methods page as the reference interaction and methodological record.
cards.engineering: Keep its existing page byte-identical during this operation.
cards.empirical: A method organizes inquiry; it does not create evidence standing.

cards.label: Applied Investigations
cards.summary: Connect the research sequence to named real systems and approved studies.
cards.practical: See why the studied problem matters in operation.
cards.engineering: Bind each investigation to its design, target, and complete record.
cards.empirical: Keep the selected study's result inside its admitted domain.

cards.label: Findings and Boundaries
cards.summary: Preserve supported, negative, mixed, unresolved, and prohibited conclusions.
cards.practical: See what was learned and where action must stop.
cards.engineering: Attach findings to exact evidence and claim ceilings.
cards.empirical: Negative and mixed findings remain first-class results.

cards.label: Source Identity
cards.summary: Name the dataset, record, observation, or artifact.
cards.practical: Make the origin understandable to a reader deciding what to trust.
cards.engineering: Bind locator, version, owner, format, and acquisition condition.
cards.empirical: Identity is necessary for evidence but is not itself validation.

cards.label: Provenance
cards.summary: Trace how the source arrived and changed.
cards.practical: Show the path from origin to the present claim.
cards.engineering: Record transformations, exclusions, hashes, custody changes, and missing steps.
cards.empirical: Untraceable transformation lowers or blocks evidentiary standing.

cards.label: Admission
cards.summary: Declare why the source belongs in this question.
cards.practical: Separate relevant material from nearby but inapplicable material.
cards.engineering: Fix inclusion, exclusion, time-window, quality, and leakage rules.
cards.empirical: Post-result admission changes make the interpretation unreliable.

cards.label: Observation
cards.summary: Separate source material from the actual unit observed.
cards.practical: Show what was counted, measured, classified, or compared.
cards.engineering: Declare observation unit, population, missingness, and dependence.
cards.empirical: Report counts and preserve negative, mixed, and absent observations.

cards.label: Claim Link
cards.summary: State how directly the source and observation support the claim.
cards.practical: Tell the reader whether the record proves, suggests, constrains, or fails to answer.
cards.engineering: Map dependencies, alternatives, and claim ceiling.
cards.empirical: Provenance and volume do not establish mechanism, transfer, or deployment fitness.
cards.boundary: Source existence is not validation; provenance and observation volume do not establish mechanism, transfer, or deployment fitness.

cards.label: Applied Problem
cards.summary: Name the real system, population, or decision being studied.
cards.practical: Explain why the problem matters beyond the page.
cards.engineering: Declare system boundary, owner, observation unit, and operating condition.
cards.empirical: Do not substitute a generic example for an admitted investigation.

cards.label: Study Question
cards.summary: Make the applied proposition answerable.
cards.practical: State what the study is trying to clarify for a real decision.
cards.engineering: Fix target, horizon, comparison, and failure condition.
cards.empirical: A useful question still requires admitted observations and a frozen design.

cards.label: Design
cards.summary: Connect source, method, comparator, and evaluation split.
cards.practical: Show how the investigation avoids learning its answer from the test itself.
cards.engineering: Preserve case separation, features, baseline, thresholds, and procedure.
cards.empirical: Evaluation standing depends on the named design, not on presentation quality.

cards.label: Bounded Result
cards.summary: State what survived evaluation inside the applied domain.
cards.practical: Explain what the result might help a person or operator notice.
cards.engineering: Bind metrics to population, target, comparator, and exact observation count.
cards.empirical: Preserve positive, stronger ordinary, negative, and mixed outcomes together.

cards.label: Complete Record
cards.summary: Continue to the canonical execution owner for full study detail.
cards.practical: Use Laws for interpretation and Frontier for complete execution custody.
cards.engineering: Do not duplicate or fork the canonical study.
cards.empirical: This page does not upgrade the selected study's evidence status.
cards.boundary: This page interprets the study for Laws; it does not reproduce the complete Frontier execution record or upgrade its evidence status.

cards.label: Supported Findings
cards.summary: Preserve the result that survived the admitted evaluation.
cards.practical: Explain the useful bounded conclusion.
cards.engineering: Attach result to target, population, metric, comparator, and receipt.
cards.empirical: Support remains inside the named domain and design.

cards.label: Negative Findings
cards.summary: Keep failed proposed measures visible.
cards.practical: Show what did not help or did not work.
cards.engineering: Preserve ablation, threshold, and component failures without repair by wording.
cards.empirical: Negative results constrain the model and the next study.

cards.label: Mixed Findings
cards.summary: Separate promising signal from unresolved interpretation.
cards.practical: Explain why a useful ranking result can coexist with a stronger ordinary explanation.
cards.engineering: Compare combined, component, baseline, and burden results.
cards.empirical: Mixed standing blocks promotion to a distinct mechanism.

cards.label: Claim Ceiling
cards.summary: State the strongest permitted conclusion and prohibited promotions.
cards.practical: Make the stopping point legible.
cards.engineering: Bind claim state to evidence and unresolved conditions.
cards.empirical: Presentation, navigation, or later implementation cannot raise the ceiling.

cards.label: Next Study
cards.summary: Turn unresolved findings into explicit future tests.
cards.practical: Show what must be learned next.
cards.engineering: Specify external replication, controls, calibration, transfer, and operational evaluation.
cards.empirical: Only newly admitted evidence can change the disposition.

cards.label: Test Object
cards.summary: Name the proposition, system, and outcome under test.
cards.practical: Make the question understandable before introducing a score.
cards.engineering: Bind target, population, horizon, and unit of evaluation.
cards.empirical: A moving test object makes later results uninterpretable.

cards.label: Admission
cards.summary: Fix what evidence and cases enter or stay out.
cards.practical: Show why each case belongs in the test.
cards.engineering: Declare inclusion, exclusion, leakage, quality, and missingness rules.
cards.empirical: Preserve excluded cases and post-admission failures.

cards.label: Baseline
cards.summary: Choose the ordinary comparison the proposition must beat or clarify.
cards.practical: Compare the new claim with what a simpler approach already provides.
cards.engineering: Freeze baseline identity, inputs, metric, and implementation before evaluation.
cards.empirical: A stronger baseline remains a controlling finding.

cards.label: Entry Receipt
cards.summary: Record the admitted state before forward construction begins.
cards.practical: Make later changes visible.
cards.engineering: Preserve source, target, split, baseline, exclusions, and fingerprints.
cards.empirical: A receipt proves custody of declarations, not scientific truth.
cards.boundary: A test is not interpretable when case admission, target definition, or baseline selection can move after results are known.

cards.label: Frozen Inputs
cards.summary: Carry only admitted evidence into construction.
cards.practical: Show what the procedure is allowed to see.
cards.engineering: Bind source version, variables, missingness, and split.
cards.empirical: Test information must remain unavailable during development.

cards.label: Procedure
cards.summary: Specify the transformation from inputs to output.
cards.practical: Explain the steps without hiding decisive choices.
cards.engineering: Freeze features, model, normalization, thresholds, and ordering.
cards.empirical: Post-result adjustment invalidates forward specification.

cards.label: Prediction
cards.summary: Declare the expected output before evaluation.
cards.practical: State what success would look like.
cards.engineering: Fix direction, metric, horizon, and acceptance threshold.
cards.empirical: Preserve misses and non-discriminating outcomes.

cards.label: Comparator
cards.summary: Run the target beside ordinary and rival explanations.
cards.practical: Show whether the new construction adds something useful.
cards.engineering: Use identical evaluation windows, metrics, and admissible inputs.
cards.empirical: A simpler stronger comparator constrains the interpretation.

cards.label: Failure Condition
cards.summary: Name what stops or invalidates the construction.
cards.practical: Make it possible for the test to fail.
cards.engineering: Declare leakage, drift, threshold, missingness, and execution stop rules.
cards.empirical: Failure is preserved rather than rewritten as success.
cards.boundary: Post-result adjustment, test leakage, or moving thresholds invalidates the claim that the construction was forward specified.

cards.label: Claim
cards.summary: Begin at the exact conclusion being preserved.
cards.practical: State what a reader might act on.
cards.engineering: Bind the claim to result, target, scope, and receipt.
cards.empirical: Do not audit a stronger claim than the evidence actually carries.

cards.label: Comparator Challenge
cards.summary: Attack the result with simpler explanations.
cards.practical: Ask whether ordinary burden explains more.
cards.engineering: Re-run baseline, burden, component, and ablation comparisons.
cards.empirical: The battery burden comparator 0.9704 remained stronger than the combined 0.9394.

cards.label: Method Trace
cards.summary: Move backward through thresholds, splits, and procedures.
cards.practical: Show where a seemingly good result could have been produced by a procedural choice.
cards.engineering: Verify fixed rules, independence, calibration, and exact execution.
cards.empirical: Preserve deviations, observer dependence, and unreproduced steps.

cards.label: Input Trace
cards.summary: Trace every evaluated value back to admitted evidence.
cards.practical: Show where the source came from.
cards.engineering: Verify identity, version, transformation, admission, and leakage controls.
cards.empirical: Missing custody weakens or blocks the conclusion.

cards.label: Audit Disposition
cards.summary: Preserve what passed, failed, and remained unresolved.
cards.practical: Explain the strongest conclusion left after challenge.
cards.engineering: Record proceed, revise, reject, hold, retest, or escalate with receipts.
cards.empirical: Mechanism, confound independence, external replication, and operational use remain open.
cards.boundary: A result that survives one held-out evaluation may still fail under confound control, transfer, independent replication, threshold calibration, source review, or operational testing.

cards.label: Result
cards.summary: State the evaluated outcome without promotion.
cards.practical: Explain what happened in the test.
cards.engineering: Bind metric, population, target, comparator, and execution identity.
cards.empirical: Report all positive, negative, mixed, and unresolved outcomes.

cards.label: Comparison
cards.summary: Place the target beside its baseline and rival explanations.
cards.practical: Show what the result adds beyond ordinary methods.
cards.engineering: Preserve identical windows, metrics, and admissible inputs.
cards.empirical: The stronger burden comparator remains visible beside the combined result.

cards.label: Failure Meaning
cards.summary: Interpret failed components and thresholds as findings.
cards.practical: Show what should not be used or assumed.
cards.engineering: Record ablation, sensitivity, zero-true-positive, and calibration failures.
cards.empirical: Failure constrains the public conclusion and next design.

cards.label: Claim Ceiling
cards.summary: Fix the strongest permitted statement.
cards.practical: Tell the reader where interpretation stops.
cards.engineering: Bind prohibited claims and review conditions to the record.
cards.empirical: Later presentation cannot raise the ceiling.

cards.label: Record
cards.summary: Preserve result, custody, and next question together.
cards.practical: Leave a durable path for inspection.
cards.engineering: Store evidence locators, procedure identity, receipts, disposition, and next test.
cards.empirical: A record documents the evaluated state; it does not create new validation.
cards.boundary: The preserved record cannot be promoted beyond its claim ceiling by later presentation, routing, or implementation.
